title: Falls and Frailty in Older Adults
lead: Falls are not a normal part of ageing. Many are preventable with the right exercise.
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Ask every older adult: "Have you fallen in the past year? How many times? Do you feel unsteady? Do you worry about falling?" For each fall: where, when, what happened, any warning (dizziness, blackout, palpitations), could you get up, how long on the floor, injuries. A fall with loss of consciousness, palpitations or chest pain is a possible syncope and needs medical assessment for cardiac causes. Do not treat it only as a balance problem.
working: Falls and Frailty in Older Adults
qa: What type of exercise reduces falls? Exercise that challenges balance, combined with strength training, done long term.
What is orthostatic hypotension? A drop in BP on standing (systolic 20 mmHg or diastolic 10 mmHg or more).
Why teach floor recovery? To prevent long lies and their complications.
What should you do if a fall involved blackout? Medical assessment for cardiac or neurological causes.
Why assess fear of falling? Fear leads to inactivity, weakness and more falls.

redFlags.Finding: Fall with blackout, palpitations, chest pain
Hip pain and inability to bear weight after a fall
Long lie (on the floor for over an hour)
Sudden new unsteadiness with neurological signs

manualNotes: Exercise that challenges balance, done regularly and for long enough, reduces falls [Ref – to verify Cochrane]. A widely used program is the Otago Exercise Programme [Ref – to verify].
Progression: reduce hand support, narrow the base, add head turns, add a cognitive task, increase repetitions and load.
Other measures: footwear advice, home hazard modification, personal alarm, vitamin D and bone health review through the doctor, continence management.
